headline: US stocks ended mixed as rotation out of tech into defensives followed easing Strait of Hormuz tensions, softer payrolls data and vigilant Fed messaging
raw_text:
- Dow Jones (DIA) Industrial Average rose, marking a third straight record close, while the S&P 500 (SPY) slipped and Nasdaq (QQQ) fell as investors rotated from recent tech winners into blue-chip and defensive names
- Progress on an Iran-Oman agreement over the Strait of Hormuz shipping route eased oil (@CL)-market and broader geopolitical tensions, supporting overall risk sentiment
- Softer-than-expected private payrolls data and Fed officials’ continued emphasis on inflation vigilance shaped rate expectations and sector positioning
- Materials and healthcare sectors led gains, while technology and communication services underperformed, and gold (@GC) prices jumped sharply
- SpaceX fell sharply despite reporting nearly doubled revenue and a strong earnings beat, as investors focused on rising AI capital expenditures and an upcoming lock-up expiration for nearly a billion shares
- AMD (AMD) declined as GF Securities and other firms raised price targets amid AI demand strength
- Eli Lilly (LLY) climbed after lifting 2026 guidance on strong revenue growth and GLP-1 momentum while agreeing to acquire AtaiBeckley
- Disney (DIS) advanced on solid theme park and entertainment results that supported consumer-related shares
- MetLife (MET) and MercadoLibre (MELI) both beat expectations, with MercadoLibre (MELI)’s quarterly sales topping $10 billion
- In after-hours trading, Motorola Solutions (MSI) rose after raising its outlook, while Western Digital (WDC) and Sandisk fell following their results, ahead of additional earnings and key economic data on Thursday
